claims.text: Groups have means 2 and 10, with counts 2 and 20. A prior mean 6 has strength 4. What is the small group’s partially pooled mean? Options: 2; 4.667; 9.273. Toy model: compare two controlled cases.
claims.source: Stipulated numerical case in model.ts, based on manager numericCase: Two groups rawmeans2and10; samplecounts2and20; sharedprior mean6strength4. Partialpooledmeans(2*2+4*6)/6=4.6667,(20*10+4*6)/24=9.3333. Completepooledweightedmean204/22=9.2727; no pooling2,10.

claims.text: A group mean 4 from two observations uses prior mean 8, strength 2. Partial mean? (2×4+2×8)/(2+2)=6.
claims.source: Transfer arithmetic or model implication under the same explicitly stated assumptions. Independent verification pending.

claims.text: Partial pooling moves the small-group mean to 4.667; complete pooling gives both groups 9.273. The large group’s partial estimate remains closer to its raw mean.

claims.text: The stipulated prior contributes four observations at mean 6. Its relative weight is larger for the group with only two observations. Partial pooling preserves differences; complete pooling erases them in this example.
